etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Middle English arbitrarie, Latin arbitrārius (“arbitrary, uncertain”), from arbiter (“witness, on-looker, listener, judge, overseer”).
senses: (usually of a decision) Based on individual discretion or judgment; not based on any objective distinction, perhaps even made at random.
Determined by impulse rather than reason; often connoting heavy-handedness.
Anything arbitrary, such as an arithmetical value or a fee.
